title: Align Python/JS/Go SDK dependencies, remove legacy API surface, and stabilize runtime deps
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Over the last 18 months each SDK (Python, JavaScript, Go) has drifted on transitive deps and internal shims. This has caused intermittent CI churn, inconsistent behavior across languages (notably around streaming and retry handling), and blocks for security patching.

Goal: Bring the three official SDKs to a consistent, minimal set of vetted runtime dependencies; remove the last legacy API surface shims that maintain backward compatibility for >2-year-old clients; and validate performance/regression impact with microbenchmarks and canary rollouts. The work should be conservative: avoid functional changes to public APIs beyond removing the documented legacy shims, provide migration tooling and docs, and gate rollout behind feature flags and compatibility tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- All 3 SDKs have dependency matrices documented and approved in Confluence.
- Python bump: requests 2.31+ and urllib3 pinned; JS bump: remove node-fetch, switch to undici for Node 18+; Go modules tidy and replace old protobuf runtime with the new stable package.
- Legacy API shims removed and corresponding deprecation notices present in CHANGELOGs and migration guide.
- CI passes with pinned deps and cross-language integration tests green.
- Performance regressions <= 5% on end-to-end 99th latency and token throughput for standard benchmarks.
- Rollout playbook and automated migration lint available in SDK repos.
- Security review completed and noted in PRs.
tasks: Inventory transitive dependencies for python/js/go and produce a compatibility matrix
Identify and mark legacy shim functions (list endpoints/classes) and map to migration surface
Create migration guide + automated codemods for JS and Python where feasible
Open language-specific PRs with pinned versions, lockfiles updates, and updated CI images
Run microbenchmarks (latency, throughput) and record baseline vs post-bump results
Coordinate with release infra to stage canary rollout and feature-flag toggles
Complete security review and add KCVs for critical libraries
Publish deprecation notes and update SDK CHANGELOGs and docs site
discussion: 2026-03-12 - Ava C: Kickoff - collected dep lists from each repo; initial concerns around node version support for undici; created compat matrix draft in Confluence (link in attachments).

2026-03-13 - Diego M: Ran local benchmarks for Python after bumping requests->2.31. Observed ~2% CPU increase on long-running streams but negligible latency impact. Added perf regression firewall in PR.
2026-03-13 - Priya (Security): Requested explicit upgrade path for grpc/protobuf in Go; flagged backward-compatibility tests for streaming RPCs. Security review queueed and prioritized.
2026-03-14 - Diego M: Opened experimental PRs: python PR #1206, js PR #842, go PR #397. Note: JS PR includes a codemod script to update users of legacy .stream() helper to new streaming API.
2026-03-14 - Sam (Docs): Will draft migration guide and a compatibility table. Needs list of removed shim function names from engineering before EOD 2026-03-16.
notes: Mitigations: keep old shims behind a runtime feature flag for a short canary period if removal causes unexpected regressions. If any language shows >5% regression we will revert that language bump and iterate. Coordinate with Solutions Engineering to notify high-usage customers listed in the dependency audit. Automation: add nightly cross-language integ test to catch future drift.
